_comment: New-publication feeds for scripts/source_watch (see its README). Every URL here was opened and parsed on 2026-10-21. A topic keyword with a capital letter matches case-sensitively; an all-lowercase one ignores case. `match` names the item fields searched (default title + summary); `books` on a feed reports every new item of that feed for those books. Vendor feeds for SailPoint and ServiceNow were opened and parsed on 2026-11-21. `exclude` on a feed is a regular expression; items whose title matches it are marked seen and not reported. A `fluidtopics_pages` feed is a weekly page check of a JavaScript-drawn documentation site (see feeds.py).

feeds.name: SailPoint SaaS release notes (Developer Community)
feeds.source: The SaaS Release Notes category of the SailPoint Developer Community (Discourse), opened and parsed on 2026-11-21. The category's own feed carries only that category, so no filter is needed; the site-wide https://developer.sailpoint.com/discuss/latest.rss mixes every category and keeps only the newest 25 topics.

feeds.name: SailPoint Identity Security Cloud API specifications
feeds.exclude: : (Update dereferenced specifications|Automated commit by github action)
feeds.source: Commits to main of https://github.com/sailpoint-oss/api-specs (the commits.atom feed of the same branch). The daily bot commits that sync the specifications are not reported; the specification files the workbook cites are watched one by one as cited sources, with their diffs.

feeds.name: SailPoint CLI releases
feeds.source: Releases of https://github.com/sailpoint-oss/sailpoint-cli (the releases.atom feed of the same repository).

feeds.name: ServiceNow SDK releases
feeds.source: Releases of https://github.com/ServiceNow/sdk (the releases.atom feed of the same repository). The SDK only; ServiceNow's platform release notes are the next feed.

feeds.name: ServiceNow family release notes (page check)
feeds.source: ServiceNow's release notes have no feed, and the docs site draws its pages with JavaScript, so a plain fetch sees only an empty shell. The page check reads the site's public Fluid Topics API instead (/api/khub/maps, then each map's toc and topic content): for every en-US release-notes publication (one per family: Xanadu, Yokohama, Zurich, Australia, Brazil on 2026-11-21) it hashes the text of the family release-notes page. A changed page, or a new family, is reported once.
